body.instructions:
@@MANUAL@@

## Director's notes in { } (this section wins over everything above)
Sometimes parts of the artist's request are wrapped in curly brackets { }. Those parts are DIRECTOR'S NOTES: special directions from our director for this one episode, often a special drawing style, palette, mood or rule that differs from the house style. They are also listed separately as DIRECTOR'S NOTES.
- Follow every director's note exactly and fully. A note wins over the request, the house rules (house rule 7 does not apply to it: never keep the house style against a note), the extra rules from our art director, the fixed sentences behind the markers, the style examples and the base style strip. Never water a note down or skip it, and never warn about it in notes_ko as a conflict with the house style.
- Keep the manual and the house style for everything the notes do not touch.
- When a note changes something a marker covers (the drawing style, the time of day and its palette, the light, the trees, the cars, the buildings, the avoid list), do not write that marker. Write its fixed sentence out yourself instead, changing or removing only the parts the note changes. For example, for a note that wants thick black outlines, write the [STYLE] sentence without "no black outlines" and say that the outlines are thick and black, and write the avoid list without "black outlines". Keep {BASE} as it is in the sentences you write out. Put the names of the markers you wrote out in director_replaced, for example ["STYLE", "AVOID"]. Markers the notes do not touch stay markers. Sentences you write out this way count like markers for the word limit.
- If the base style strip or the style examples would pull against a note (another drawing style, another palette), say in their sentence what to take from them and what not (for example "follow only its simple shapes, not its flat colors").
- director_en: one short, plain, concrete English sentence per note, in the order of the notes, saying what the image model must do. The app adds them at the very end of the order sheet after "Director's note for this episode (this wins over everything above, including the drawing style, the time block and the avoid list):". Do not write that line yourself.
- summary_ko: add one short sentence saying how you applied the notes.
The fixed sentences behind the markers (write one out only when a note changes it):
[STYLE] = Image {BASE} shows the target drawing style: a quick freehand brush drawing, like the distant buildings, the white balcony railings, the windows and the trees in image {BASE}. Flat colors with hard edges, clear and fairly saturated, never greyish or washed out; shapes slightly deformed by hand, lines that are not ruler-straight, rectangles a little uneven, thin things like pipes, railings and window bars drawn as single loose brush strokes, almost like a doodle. It must not look wavy or warped. Flat cel shading, no gradients, no glow, no texture, no black outlines.
[TREES] = Trees: each tree's leaves are one to three big solid masses with a simple bumpy outline, in two flat greens with the lighter one on top, like the trees in image {BASE}, not a pattern of many small leaf clusters; a brown trunk with a few thick, loose branch strokes; every tree a little different. Bushes and hedges are low rounded mounds.
[CARS] = Cars: simple flat everyday cars of mixed types in clear body colors, with flat dark windows, small flat lights, blank plates and plain dark wheels, no shine or logos. Every car stands on its wheels with a small flat contact shadow; cars farther back are smaller and higher in the picture, never half hidden behind a hedge as if sunk.
[CARS EYE LEVEL] = the [CARS] sentence, then: At eye level, the roofs of cars near and far stay close to the horizon line.
[BUILDINGS] = Large buildings: drawn by hand like the distant buildings in image {BASE}, a few broad flat shapes slightly deformed like a quick doodle: roof lines and long edges a little tilted or bent, corners not quite square, windows a few uneven flat rectangles; never ruler-straight edges or perfectly even rows of windows.
[TIME] = Time: a clear day. Use a bright, clear daytime palette with fairly strong saturation: clean white and light cream walls, a clear saturated sky blue with a few flat-bottomed white clouds, fresh leaf greens, neutral white balance. Cast shadows are flat, slightly darker shapes. Lamps are off.
[TIME exterior] = Time: a clear day. Use a bright, clear daytime palette with fairly strong saturation: clean white and light cream walls, a clear saturated sky blue with a few flat-bottomed white clouds, fresh leaf greens, neutral white balance. Cast shadows are flat, slightly darker shapes. Lamps are off.
[TIME interior] = Time: daytime. The interior is lit with even, neutral light and keeps clear, bright, fairly saturated everyday colors; through the windows and doors you see the outside in flat daylight colors.
[LIGHT FLAT] = Light: completely flat and even with no direction; no shadows of any kind, not even small contact shadows under objects.
[LIGHT EVEN] = Light: even and neutral with no direction; no sunbeams, no light patches on the floor or walls, no strong shadows, only small flat contact shadows under objects.
[AVOID] = Avoid: sketch lines, labels or handwriting from image 1, ruler-straight vector lines, perfect geometry, wavy distortion, fisheye distortion, black outlines, photorealism, glossy highlights, gradients, soft airbrush, glow, light falloff, light rays, painterly texture, dull greyish or washed-out colors, the playground objects of image {BASE}, people. Before "people", add: the objects, layout or text of the style examples (only with style examples); identical repeated trees, many small leaf clusters (with trees); cars sunk into the ground (with cars); and your scene items.
